claims.text: Removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi increases the effective stacking-fault energy of the resulting FeNiCrMn alloy.
Higher stacking-fault energy suppresses the nucleation of deformation twins.
Higher stacking-fault energy shifts the dominant deformation mechanism toward dislocation glide.
The twin-to-dislocation-glide shift changes the strain-rate sensitivity and temperature dependence of yield strength and work hardening.
The Co-free alloy's dynamic strength–ductility response will differ from that of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The starting Co-free FeNiCrMn material is a solidified, single-phase FCC solid solution.
The comparison changes the composition from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi to Co-free FeNiCrMn while holding processing and testing variables constant.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi typically has lower stacking-fault energy than the Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy.
The lower stacking-fault energy of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi promotes deformation twinning under dynamic loading.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will develop a lower density of deformation twins.
Relative to the baseline, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have a measurably modified yield-strength and strain-rate-sensitivity profile.
At higher strain rates, the Co-free alloy may exhibit higher yield strength because of enhanced dislocation-mediated hardening.
The hypothesis is restricted to homogeneous FCC solid solutions tested without deformation-induced phase transformations.
Stacking-fault energy can depend strongly on temperature and local chemical short-range order.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi exhibits strain-rate-dependent dynamic behavior involving moving dislocations and dynamic strain aging at intermediate temperatures.
Identically processed tensile specimens tested at 10^-3, 10^-1, and 10^3 s^-1, with TEM or EBSD characterization, provide a controlled comparison of the two alloys.

contradictions.description: The prediction only requires a modified response and states higher high-rate yield strength as a possibility, whereas the falsification rule treats an inferior response as falsifying. An inferior but measurably different response could satisfy the broad prediction, so it is not intrinsically decisive against the proposed SFE mechanism.
